#             BUS BUDDY

# ABSTRACT

Ensuring student safety and preventing bus overcrowding are vital responsibilities for college transport management. Overcrowded college buses violate transport compliance guidelines and make manual roll-calling time-consuming and unreliable. Additionally, transit fire accidents caused by electrical wiring faults or overheated engine compartments present grave dangers during daily student commutes. This project proposes an automated, embedded monitoring system tailored for institutional college buses. Built using an Arduino Uno microcontroller, the system provides automated bidirectional headcount tracking and active cabin smoke monitoring. An Infrared (IR) sensor installed at the front boarding door registers entering students, while an Ultrasonic sensor positioned at the exit door registers students alighting. Concurrently, an MQ-series smoke sensor continuously monitors the passenger cabin. If smoke or fire is detected, the microcontroller instantly triggers an alert buzzer to instruct the driver to halt the bus and facilitate an immediate student evacuation.

## INTRODUCTION & PROBLEM STATEMENT

## College transport networks operate on strict time schedules across fixed bus routes, picking up and dropping off students at designated stops. Managing student counts manually poses several everyday hurdles:

## 

## Overcrowding & Safety Violations: Drivers and bus coordinators cannot reliably count boarding students during peak morning rushes, often resulting in students standing beyond safe vehicle capacity.

## 

## Lost Transit Time: Manual attendance counting at every campus gate or pickup point causes transit delays.

## 

## Fire & Electrical Hazards: College buses run long suburban routes under high engine loads, where wire degradation or battery short circuits can lead to sudden cabin fires.

## 

## By combining an IR sensor for boarding detection, an ultrasonic sensor for exit detection, and an onboard smoke sensor with an acoustic alarm, this project automates student transit accounting and guarantees early fire hazard mitigation on college transport fleets

### 

### OBJECTIVES

To build a dedicated embedded safety prototype designed for institutional college buses.

To detect and increment the onboard student count automatically as students board the college bus using an IR sensor.

To detect and decrement the student count as students get off at their designated campus or route stops using an ultrasonic sensor.

To maintain an accurate, real-time count of total students inside the vehicle to prevent exceeding statutory seat capacities.

To continuously sniff cabin air for combustible gas leaks and smoke emissions.

To sound an immediate emergency buzzer alarm to ensure swift vehicle evacuation before fire spreads.

#### 4\. HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS

## 1\)  Arduino Uno / Nano (Main Controller):

## Coordinates inputs from the entry, exit, and smoke detection modules.

## Calculates the net student occupancy variable (studentCount) and asserts output triggers.

## 

## 2\) Infrared (IR) Sensor Module:

## Mounted at the front footboard entrance.

## Emits an infrared signal and registers a LOW digital trigger when a student interrupts the optical path while stepping into the bus.

## 

## 3\) Ultrasonic Sensor (HC-SR04):

## Positioned at the exit doorway or descent step.

## Emits ultrasonic pulses (40 kHz) to calculate clearance distance. When an alighting student breaks the doorway distance threshold, the sensor registers an exit event.

## 

## 4\) Smoke Sensor (MQ-2 / MQ-135):

## Installed inside the bus cabin ceiling (near the engine compartment bulkhead or middle ceiling).

## Detects combustible gases, smoke particles, and electrical smoldering.

## 5\) Piezoelectric Buzzer:

## Functions as an acoustic alarm on the driver's dashboard to mandate an immediate stop and passenger evacuation.

## 6\) Power Regulation Module:

## 9V/12V DC input stepped down to a stable 5V DC supply for the microcontroller and sensors.

## Pin Interfacing Table: 

IR Sensor (Entrance): VCC \-\> 5V, GND \-\> GND, OUT \-\> Pin D2

Ultrasonic Sensor (Exit): VCC \-\> 5V, GND \-\> GND, TRIG \-\> Pin D3, ECHO \-\> Pin D4

Smoke Sensor (Cabin): VCC \-\> 5V, GND \-\> GND, DO \-\> Pin D7 (or AO \-\> Pin A0)

Buzzer (Alarm): Positive (+) \-\> Pin D8, Negative (-) \-\> GND

##### WORKING PRINCIPLE IN COLLEGE BUS OPERATIONS:

1)Morning Boarding (Ingress Detection):

At each designated pickup stop, students board through the front entrance.  
When a student steps up, their leg or body breaks the IR beam.  
The IR module sends a digital LOW transition to pin D2. The Arduino detects this edge, increments studentCount by 1 (studentCount++), and holds a 500 ms software debounce delay to prevent counting the same student twice.

2)Campus Arrival & Alighting (Egress Detection):

Once the bus arrives at the college campus drop-off bay, students alight via the exit door.  
The ultrasonic sensor continuously calculates the distance to the opposite door panel.  
As a student steps through, their body decreases the measured distance below the calibrated exit threshold (e.g., \< 50 cm).  
The Arduino detects this distance reduction and decrements studentCount by 1 (studentCount--), ensuring the count never drops below zero.

3)Cabin Fire & Smoke Monitoring:

Electrical short circuits or engine bay issues can release toxic fumes or smoke into the passenger compartment.  
The MQ smoke sensor's conductivity rises with increasing smoke concentration.  
Once the smoke density exceeds the safe threshold, pin D7 shifts to an active state. The Arduino immediately energizes the dashboard buzzer (pin D8 set to HIGH), alerting the college bus driver to stop immediately and direct the students out through emergency exits.

8\. ADVANTAGES SPECIFIC TO COLLEGE BUSES  
Prevents Overcrowding: College transport officers can define a maximum passenger limit matching vehicle seat quotas.  
Accurate Transport Accounting: Eliminates the manual burden for student coordinators verifying roll sheets on moving vehicles.

Rapid Hazard Evacuation: Gives the driver instant, audible notice if smoke emerges from bus.

Low Budget & High Reliability: Uses affordable, solid-state sensors requiring very low electrical draw from the bus battery.
